children.value: The Nelson-Siegel model is a workhorse in fixed-income finance. Its true power lies in its ability to take a discrete, often noisy set of market observations and translate them into a continuous, smooth yield curve that accurately reflects market expectations.
The next volume focuses on several applications of the model, including:

Because Nelson-Siegel provides a continuous discount function, it allows practitioners to interpolate and extrapolate yields for any specific, non-standard maturity date. This is absolutely critical for pricing off-the-run bonds, structuring Forward Rate Agreements (FRAs), and bootstrapping zero-coupon curves for swap valuation where cash flows occur on highly specific dates.
Traditional Modified Duration assumes a parallel shift in the yield curve - a rarity in the real world. The Nelson-Siegel framework moves beyond basic duration to calculate

focusing on changes in the level, slope, and curvature of the term structure. This more granular view enhances the understanding of a bond portfolio’s risk profile and allows investors to make focused bets on rate changes
